en: 99) Jesus appeared not long before the last crisis which the fermentation of the manifold elements of the Jewish fate drew on.

In this time of inner fermentation, of the development of this various material, until it is gathered into a whole and the pure oppositions, open war, arise, several partial outbreaks preceded the last act.

Human beings of a commoner soul, but of strong passions, grasped the fate of the Jewish people only incompletely, and were therefore not calm enough either to let themselves be carried along by its waves without consciousness and to swim along only with the time, or to await further development, which would have been necessary in order to ally themselves with a greater power; [so] they ran ahead of the fermentation of the whole and fell without honour and without effect.
zh: 99) 耶稣出场，离那场把犹太命运的各种要素的发酵引来的最后危机已经不久。
在这内在发酵的时期，在这各种材料的展开之中——直到它被聚集成一个整体、纯粹的对立、公开的战争产生出来——最后那一幕之前还有过好几次局部的爆发。
灵魂比较平庸、激情却强烈的人，只不完整地领会犹太民族的命运，因此也不够平静，既不能毫无意识地让命运的波浪把自己带走、只随时间往前漂，也不能等待那本来必要的进一步发展，好让自己傍上一个更大的力量；〔于是〕他们抢在整个发酵的前头，落得既无荣誉又无效果。

en: Jesus fought not only one part of the Jewish fate, because he was not caught up in another part of it, but set himself against the whole; was therefore himself exalted above it and sought to exalt his people above it.

But such hostilities, in so far as he sought to sublate them, can only be overcome by bravery, not reconciled by love; for that reason his sublime attempt to overcome the whole of fate had to fail among his people, and he himself had to become a victim of it.

Because Jesus had not taken the side of any part of fate, his religion, to be sure not among his people, for this still possessed too much, but in the rest of the world, had to find so great an entrance among human beings who had no share any more in that fate, who had nothing at all to defend or to assert.
zh: 耶稣所打击的不只是犹太命运的一部分，因为他并没有被这命运的另一部分缠住，而是把自己摆到了整体的对面；所以他本人就高居于这整体之上，并且设法把他的民族也提升到这整体之上。
但这类敌意，就他把它们扬弃而言，只有靠勇敢才能制伏，不能靠爱来和解；所以他那个克服命运整体的崇高尝试，也就必然在他的民族里失败，而他本人则成了这命运的牺牲品。
因为耶稣没有倒向命运的任何一边，所以他的宗教虽然不是在他的民族里，因为这个民族还占有太多，而是在其余的世界里，必然在这样一些人那里找到如此之大的入口：他们于这命运已不再有一份，根本没有什么要辩护、要坚持。

en: Before the Spirit of Christ100)
zh: 在基督的精神面前100)

en: [on a] living modification of human nature (rights which he himself gives up when he establishes powers over himself) might recognize, were commanded to them, were for them through and through positive.

The order in which here the different kinds of legislation of the Jews are followed is therefore one foreign to them, a made order, and the differences enter into it only through the way in which there is a different reaction to it.
zh: 植根于人性的一种活的变形（他一旦把种种权力设定在自己之上，就自己放弃了那些权利）可能认识到，这些诫命对他们来说是被命令的，对他们来说完全是实证的。
这里跟在犹太人各种不同类型的立法后面走的那种次序，因此是一种对他们陌生的、做出来的次序，而那些差别进入其中，靠的只是人们对它作出不同反应的方式。

en: To the commandments which demanded a mere service of the Lord, an immediate bondage, an obedience without joy, without pleasure and love, that is, to the divine-service commandments, Jesus opposed the directly opposite of them, a drive, even a need of the human being.

Since religious actions are the most spiritual, the most beautiful, are that which also seeks to unite the separations made necessary by development, and to present the union in the ideal as utterly existing, no longer opposed to actuality, that is, to express and confirm it in an action, religious actions are, if they lack that spirit of beauty, the emptiest; the most senseless bondage, which demands a consciousness of its annihilation; an action in which the human being expresses his being-nothing, his passivity; and the satisfaction of the commonest human need is exalted above these, because in it, to be sure, there still lies immediately the feeling or the preservation of an existence, even if an empty one.
zh: 对于那些只要求侍奉主、要求一种直接的奴役、要求一种没有快乐、没有乐趣和爱的服从的诫命，也就是说，对于礼拜的诫命，耶稣摆出了与它们正相反对的东西，即人的一种冲动，甚至一种需要。

既然宗教行动是最精神的、最美的，是那种连发展所造成的种种分离也还要去结合、并且力图把这种结合在理想中表现为完全存在着的、不再与现实性相对立的东西，也就是说，力图在一种行动中把它表达出来、把它确认下来，那么，宗教行动一旦缺少了那种美的精神，就是最空洞的；是最没有意义的奴役，它要求一种对自己被消灭的意识；是一种行动，人在其中表达自己的不存在、自己的被动；而最粗俗的人类需要的满足还高居于这些之上，因为在这种满足里，毕竟直接就有一种感觉，或一种即使空洞的存在之保存。

en: That the highest need violates what is holy is an identical proposition, for the need is a state of being torn apart, and an action that violates a holy object is the need in action.
In need, either the human being is made into an object and suppressed, or he must make nature into an object and suppress it.

Not only nature is holy; there can also be holy things that are objects in themselves, not only when they themselves are presentations of an ideal that unites many, but [also when they] stand in some relation to it, belong to it.

Need can command the desecration of such a holy thing; but to violate it without need is wantonness, if that in which a people is united is at the same time something common, a property of all; for then the violation of the sanctuary is at the same time an unjust violation of the right of all; the pious zeal that smashes the temples and altars of a foreign divine service, drives out its priests, desecrates sanctuaries that are common and belong to all.

But if a holy thing unites all only in so far as all renounce, in so far as all serve, then everyone who separates himself from [the] others takes up his right over it again, and the violation of such a holy thing or commandment is, with respect to the others, a disturbance only in so far as community with them is renounced and the arbitrary use of what is one's own - be it this time, or whatever it is - is again vindicated for oneself.

But the smaller such a right and the sacrifice of it is, the less will a human being on that account set himself against his fellow citizens in what is highest to them, want to tear apart the community with them at the most intimate point of the bond.

Only when the whole of the community is an object of contempt - and since Jesus stepped out of the whole existence of his people, this kind of forbearance fell away, with which otherwise a friend in indifferent matters limits himself toward the one with whom he is one heart and one soul, and for the sake of a Jewish holiness he did not refuse, did not even postpone the satisfaction of a very common need, of an arbitrary whim; he let his separation from his people, his whole contempt for the bondage under objective commandments, be read in that.
zh: 最高的困厄会侵犯神圣的东西，这是一个同一的命题，因为困厄是一种被撕裂的状态，而一个侵犯神圣对象的行动就是行动中的困厄。
在困厄中，要么人被弄成对象并受到压制，要么他必须把自然弄成对象并加以压制。
不只是自然神圣；也可能有本身即是对象的神圣之物，不只是当它们本身是一个把许多东西联合起来的献身的理想的呈现时，而是〔当它们〕以某种方式与这个理想相关、属于这个理想时，也是这样。
困厄可以命令人去亵渎这样一件神圣的东西；但没有困厄而去侵犯它，就是任意妄为——如果一个民族在其中结合起来的东西同时是共同的东西、是所有人共有的财产；因为这样一来，对圣物的侵犯同时就是对所有人权利的不公正侵犯；那种虔诚的狂热砸碎异教礼拜的庙宇和祭坛、赶走它的祭司，就是在亵渎共同的、属于所有人的圣物。
但若一个神圣之物之所以把所有人结合起来，只是因为所有人都放弃、所有人都侍奉，那么，每一个把自己与〔其他〕人分开的人，就重新拾回了自己在这上面的权利，而侵犯这样一件神圣之物或诫命，就其他人而言，只在这样的限度内是一种扰乱：他放弃了与他们的共同体，并且重新为自己索回了对自己东西的任意使用——不管这东西是时间，还是别的什么。
但这样一种权利以及为它所作的牺牲越微不足道，人就越不会为了它而在同胞心中最高的东西上与他们作对，越不会想在联结最内在的那一点上扯断与他们的共同体。
只有当整个共同体成了蔑视的对象时——而既然耶稣走出了他民族的全部存在，这种体谅也就没有了，平时一个朋友在无关紧要的事情上还会用它来约束自己、不去冒犯那个与他同心同德的人——他也不会为了一种犹太人的神圣性而放弃，甚至不肯推后一种极粗俗需要的满足、一种任意之举；他就在这上面让人读出他与自己民族的分裂，读出他对受客观诫命奴役的全部蔑视。

en: His companions gave the Jews offence by plucking the ears of grain on the Sabbath; the hunger that drove them to it could find no great satisfaction in those ears; reverence for the Sabbath could surely have postponed this slight satisfaction by the time they needed to reach a place where they could find prepared food.

Jesus holds David up to the Pharisees, who censured that unlawful action, but this man had grasped after the showbread in the extremest need; he also adduces the desecration of the Sabbath by priestly business; but since these are lawful, they are no desecration of it; and while on one side he magnifies the transgression itself by the remark that the priests desecrate the Sabbath only in the temple, but that here there was still more, that nature is holier than the temple, he on the other side in general exalts the nature that is godless and unholy for the Jews above their restriction of the world, which stands in relation to God, to a single place made by the Jews; but immediately he sets the human being against the hallowing of a time and declares the former to be lower than an indifferent satisfaction of a human need.

On the same day Jesus heals a withered hand; the Jews' own way of acting with regard to a beast in danger proves to them, to be sure, as does David's use of the holy bread or the priests' business on the Sabbath, that the holiness of this day does not count as absolute even for them, that they themselves know something higher than the observance of this commandment; but the case too that he here holds up to the Jews is a case of need, and need wipes out the guilt.

The animal that falls into the pit requires immediate help - but whether that man also went without the use of his hand until sunset was entirely indifferent; Jesus' action expressed the arbitrariness of performing this action a few hours earlier, and the primacy of such arbitrariness over a commandment that proceeds from the highest authority.
zh: 他的同伴们在安息日掐麦穗，给了犹太人一个冒犯；驱使他们这样做的饥饿，在那些麦穗里并不能得到多大的满足；对安息日的敬畏本来满可以把这点微小的满足推迟到他们走到一个能找到现成食物的地方所需的那段时间。

耶稣对那些责备这一不被允许的行为的法利赛人举出大卫来，但大卫是在极端的困厄中才去抓那些陈设饼的；他又举出祭司的事务对安息日的亵渎；可是，既然这些是合法的，它们就不是对安息日的亵渎；而当他一方面用这句话把过失本身放大，即祭司只是在圣殿里才亵渎安息日，而这里还有更多的东西、自然比圣殿更神圣，他另一方面就在总体上把那种对犹太人来说没有神、不神圣的自然，抬到了他们对世界所作的限制之上——他们把与世界相关、与上帝相关的世界限制在犹太人做出来的一个地点上；但他紧接着又把人与一个时间的圣化对立起来，并且宣布后者比一种无关紧要的人类需要之满足更低。
同一天耶稣治好了一只枯干的手；犹太人自己在对待一头处于危险中的牲畜时的做法，固然向他们证明，就像大卫动用圣饼或祭司在安息日的事务所证明的那样，这一天的神圣性对他们自己也不是绝对的，他们自己也知道有比遵守这条诫命更高的东西；但他在这里举给犹太人看的那个情形，也正是一个困厄的情形，而困厄抹掉了罪责。
掉进坑里的牲畜需要立刻救助——但那个人是否也要到日落才用上自己的手，则完全无所谓；耶稣的行动表达出的是提前几个钟头做这件事的任意，以及这样一种任意对一条出自最高权威的诫命的优先。

en: To the practice of washing the hands before eating bread, Jesus (Matth.
15, 2) opposes the whole subjectivity of the human being, and against the bondage to something commanded, [against] the purity or impurity of an object, the purity or impurity of the heart.
He made the indeterminate subjectivity, the character, into a wholly different sphere, which has nothing at all in common with the punctual following of objective commandments.
zh: 对于吃饼前洗手的做法，耶稣（《马太福音》
15, 2）摆出的是人的整个主体性，并且把心的纯洁或不纯洁摆到对一条被命令之物的奴役、摆到一个对象的纯洁或不纯洁的对面。
他把那不确定的主体性、把性格，弄成了一个完全不同的领域，这个领域与一板一眼地遵从客观诫命毫无共同之处。

en: Differently than toward the purely objective commandments, to which Jesus opposed something wholly foreign, the subjective in general, Jesus behaved toward those laws that we, from different points of view, call either moral or civil commandments101).
Since they express natural relations of man in the form of commandments, the aberration with regard to them consists in this, that they become either wholly or in part objective.

Since laws are unions of opposites in a concept that thus leaves them as opposites, but the concept itself consists in the opposition to something actual, it expresses an ought; insofar as the concept is considered not according to its content but according to its form, that it is a concept made and grasped by man, the commandment is moral; insofar as only the content is looked at, as the determinate union of determinate opposites, and the ought therefore does not stem from the property of the concept but is asserted by a foreign power, insofar the commandment is civil.

Because in the latter respect the union of the opposites is not comprehended, not subjective, civil laws contain the limit of the opposition of several living beings — but the purely moral ones determine the limit of the opposition within one living being; the former therefore restrict the opposition of living beings against living beings, the latter the opposition of one side, one force of a living being against other sides, other forces of that very same living being102); and one force of this being is in this respect dominant against another force of the same.

Purely moral laws that are not capable of becoming civil, i.e. in which the opposites and the union cannot have the form of something foreign, would be those that concern the restriction of such forces whose activity is not an activity, a relation toward other human beings.

The laws, when they are effective as merely civil commandments, are positive, and because they are equal to moral ones according to their matter, or because the union of something objective in the concept also presupposes a non-objective one or can become such, it would be the sublation of the form of civil laws if they were made into moral ones, if their ought were not the command of a foreign power but the consequence of their own concept, respect for duty.

But even those moral commandments that are not capable of becoming civil can become objective through this, that the union (or restriction) does not itself work as concept, as commandment, but as something foreign to the restricted force, although also something subjective.
This kind of objectivity could be sublated only through the restoration of the concept itself and of the restriction of activity through it.

In this way one could expect that Jesus would have worked against the positivity of moral commandments, against mere legality, that he would have shown that the legal is something universal and its whole obligatoriness lies in its universality, because on the one hand every ought, everything commanded indeed announces itself as something foreign, but on the other hand as concept (the universality) is something subjective, whereby it loses its objectivity, its positivity, heteronomy, as the product of a human force, of the capacity for the universal, of reason, and the commanded presents itself as grounded in an autonomy of the human will.

Through this course, however, positivity is only in part taken away103); and between the Tungusian shaman with the European prelate governing church and state, or the Mogul with the Puritan and the one obeying his duty-commandment, the difference is not that the former made themselves slaves, the latter would be free104); but that the former carries the master outside himself, the latter however carries the master within himself, yet at the same time is his own slave; for the particular, drives, inclinations, pathological love, sensuousness, or whatever one calls it, the universal is necessarily and eternally something foreign, something objective; an indestructible positivity remains left over, which becomes utterly revolting through this, that the content that the universal duty-commandment receives, a determinate duty, contains the contradiction of being restricted and universal at the same time and for the sake of the form of universality makes the harshest pretensions on account of its one-sidedness.

Woe to the human relations that are not found precisely in the concept of duty, which, as soon as it is not merely the empty thought of universality but is to present itself in an action, excludes or dominates all other relations.
zh: 对于纯粹的客观诫命，耶稣拿一种完全陌生的东西、即一般说来主观的东西去与之相对，而他对待那些我们按不同角度或者称为道德的、或者称为市民的诫命的法律，却是另一种态度101)。
因为它们把人的自然关系表达为诫命的形式，所以在它们身上的迷误就在于：它们或者全部、或者部分地变成客观的。
既然法律是对立者在概念中的结合，而这个概念让它们仍然作为对立者，概念本身却又存在于对现实的东西的对立之中，所以它表达的是一个应当；就概念不是按其内容、而是按其形式、即它是被人制作和把握的概念来看，诫命是道德的；就只着眼于内容、即作为确定的对立者的确定的结合，因而这个应当并非来自概念的性质、而是由一种陌生的权力所主张来看，诫命就是市民的。
因为在后一种角度下，对立者的结合没有被把握、不是主观的，所以市民的法律包含多个活生生的东西之间对立的界限——而纯粹道德的法律则规定一个活生生的东西之内对立的界限；前者限制的是活生生的东西对活生生的东西的对立，后者限制的是一个活生生的东西的一个方面、一种力量对同一个活生生的东西的其他方面、其他力量的对立102)；而这一本质的一种力量在这种意义上是统治着同一本质的另一种力量的。
纯粹道德的法律，如果它们不能成为市民的法律，也就是说，在它们那里对立者和结合不能具有陌生的东西的形式，那就只能是这样的法律：它们涉及的是这样一些力量的限制，这些力量的活动不是一种活动、不是一种对其他人的关系。
这些法律，当它们仅仅作为市民的诫命而有效时，就是实证的；又因为它们按自己的材料是与道德的诫命相同的，或者因为客观的东西在概念中的结合也以某种非客观的东西为前提、或者能够成为这样一种东西，所以，如果它们被造成道德的诫命，如果它们的应当不是一种陌生权力的命令，而是它们自己概念的后果、是对义务的敬重，那就是市民法律的形式的扬弃。
但就连那些不能成为市民诫命的道德诫命，也能由此变成客观的：结合（或限制）本身不是作为概念、作为诫命起作用，而是作为对被限制的力量来说陌生的东西起作用，尽管它同时又是主观的东西。
这种客观性只能通过恢复概念本身、以及通过概念对活动的限制，才可能被扬弃。

这样一来，人们倒可以指望耶稣是针对道德诫命的实证性、针对单纯的合法性而工作的，指望他表明：合法性的东西是一个普遍的东西，它的全部约束力都在于它的普遍性；因为一方面，每一个应当、每一个被命令的东西虽然都作为陌生的东西宣告自己，另一方面它作为概念（普遍性）又是主观的东西，从而作为人的一种力量、即普遍性的能力、理性的产物，失去它的客观性、它的实证性、他律性，而被命令的东西就表现为奠基在人的意志的一种自律之中。

但经过这一进程，实证性只是部分地被拿掉了103)；而在通古斯人的萨满与统治教会和国家的欧洲高级教士之间，或者在莫卧儿人与清教徒、与那个服从自己义务诫命的人之间，区别并不在于前者把自己变成了奴隶、后者是自由的104)；区别在于：前者把主人背在自己身外，后者却把主人背在自己身内，但同时又是我自己的奴隶；对于特殊的东西，即冲动、偏好、病态的爱、感性，或者人们随便叫它什么，普遍的东西必然地、永恒地是一种陌生的东西、一种客观的东西；总还剩下一种不可摧毁的实证性，而它之所以变得彻底令人愤慨，是因为普遍义务诫命所获得的内容、即一种确定的义务，含有既受限制又同时是普遍的矛盾，并且为了普遍性这一形式的缘故，为着自己的片面性提出最苛刻的要求。
人类的关系，凡是并不正好在义务的概念里找得到的，就有祸了：因为义务的概念只要不只是普遍性这一空洞思想，而是要在一种行为中表现出来，它就把所有其他关系都排除掉或者统治起来。

en: A man who wanted to restore man in his wholeness could impossibly take such a path, which only adds a stubborn conceit to the tornness of man.

To act in the spirit of the laws could not mean for him to act out of respect for duty with contradiction of the inclinations; for both parts of the spirit (one cannot speak otherwise with this tornness of the mind) would precisely thereby not be in the spirit at all, but against the spirit of the laws, the one because it is an excluding, thus self-restricted one, the other because it is a suppressed one.
zh: 一个想要把人重新恢复为其整体的人，绝不可能走上这样一条路，那条路只会给人的分裂再添上一种固执的狂妄。
按法律的精神去行动，对他来说不可能意味着出于对义务的敬重、带着偏好的矛盾去行动；因为精神的这两个部分（在心灵如此分裂的情况下人们不能换一种说法）恰恰因此根本不在精神里，而是违反法律的精神的：一部分因为它是一个排除性的、因而自受限定的部分，另一部分因为它是一个被压抑的部分。

en: Immediately turned against laws, this spirit of Jesus exalted above morality shows itself in the Sermon on the Mount, which is an attempt carried through on several examples of laws to take away from the laws the legal, the form of laws, which does not preach respect for them but points out that which fulfils them, yet as laws sublates them, and is thus something higher than obedience to them and makes them dispensable.

Since the duty-commandments presuppose a separation and the dominion of the concept announces itself in an ought, by contrast that which is exalted above this separation is a being, a modification of life, which is excluding, thus restricted, only when considered with regard to the object, since the exclusion is given only through the restrictedness of the object and concerns only the same.

Even if Jesus also expresses as commandments that which he sets against the laws and above them (Think not that I would abolish the law; Let your word be; I say to you, not to resist, etc.; Love God and your neighbour), this turn is commandment in a wholly different sense than the ought of the duty-commandment; it is only the consequence of this, that the living is thought, spoken, given in the form of the concept foreign to it, whereas the duty-commandment is by its essence, as something universal, a concept.

And if thus the living appears in the form of something reflected, something said, before men, then Kant105) was very wrong to regard this manner of expression, which does not belong to the living: Love God above all and your neighbour as yourself, as a commandment that demands respect for a law that commands love.

And on this confusion of the duty-commandment, which consists in the opposition of the concept and the actual, and the wholly unessential manner of uttering the living, rests his profound reduction of that which he calls a commandment: Love God above all and your neighbour as yourself, to his duty-commandment.

And his remark that love — or in the meaning that he thinks he must give to this love: gladly to perform all duties — cannot be commanded, falls away of itself, because in love all thought of duties falls away; and also the honour that he again lets that saying of Jesus receive in return, to regard it as the ideal of holiness unattainable by any creature, is just as superfluously squandered; for such an ideal, in which the duties would be represented as gladly done, is in itself contradictory, because duties required an opposition and the gladly-done no opposition; and he can endure this contradiction without union in his ideal by declaring rational creatures (a curious combination) capable of falling, but incapable of attaining that ideal.
zh: 这种超越道德之上的耶稣精神，直接针对法律表现出来，是在山上宝训里：那篇宝训在若干法律的例子上做了一番尝试，要取掉法律身上合法性的东西、即法律的形式；它不是宣讲对法律的敬重，而是指出那使法律得到充实、但作为法律又把它们扬弃的东西，因而它是比服从法律更高的东西，并使法律成为可以缺少的。
既然义务诫命以分离为前提，概念在一种应当中的统治也由此宣告自己，那么与此相反，超越这种分离的东西是一种存在、生命的一种变状，它只有在就客体来考察时才是排除性的、因而是受限制的，因为这种排除只是由客体的受限性给出的，并且只涉及这同一个客体。
即使耶稣也把他置于法律对面、置于法律之上的东西表达为诫命（不要以为我来是要废除法律；你们的话应当是；我告诉你们，不要抵抗，等等；爱上帝并爱你的邻人），这一转向作为诫命，与义务诫命的应当处在完全不同的意义上；它只是这样一个事实的后果：活生生的东西被思想、被说出、被放到对它陌生的概念形式里；与此相反，义务诫命按其本质作为普遍的东西就是一个概念。
而如果活生生的东西就这样以被反思的、被说出的形式出现在人面前，那么康德105)就很没有道理，把这种并不属于活生生的东西的表达方式——“你要尽心爱上帝，并爱你的邻人如同自己”——看作一条诫命，这条诫命要求对一条命令爱的法律表示敬重。
而他的那种深刻做法就建立在这一混淆之上：把义务诫命（它存在于概念与现实的东西的对立之中）与那种完全非本质的、说出活生生的东西的方式混淆起来，从而把他称为诫命的那句话——“你要尽心爱上帝，并爱你的邻人如同自己”——归结为他的义务诫命。

至于他的那个评论，说爱——或者按他以为必须赋予这种爱的意义来说：乐意履行一切义务——不能被命令，这个评论自己就站不住了，因为在爱里，关于义务的一切思想都消失了；而他反过来让耶稣那句话得到的那种荣誉，即把它看作任何造物都达不到的圣洁理想，同样是被多余地浪费掉了；因为这样一个理想——在其中义务被表象为乐意履行的——本身就是自相矛盾的，因为义务要求一种对立，而乐意履行并不要求任何对立；而他能在自己的理想里忍受这种没有结合的矛盾，办法是宣布理性的造物（一个奇怪的搭配）能够堕落，却宣布它们达不到那个理想。

en: Jesus begins the Sermon on the Mount with a kind of paradoxes in which his full soul at once declares unambiguously to the crowd of expectant listeners that from him they have to expect something wholly foreign, another genius, another world.

They are cries in which he, inspired, at once removes himself from the common estimation of virtue, inspired announces another right and light, another region of life, whose relation to the world can only be that of being hated and persecuted by it.

In this kingdom of God, however, he shows them not the dissolution of the laws, but they must be fulfilled through a righteousness that is another, in which there is more, that is more complete than the righteousness of the duty-men: a filling up of what is defective in the laws.
zh: 耶稣以一类悖论开始山上宝训，在那些悖论里，他充实的灵魂立刻向那群期待着的听众毫不含糊地宣告：他们从他那里要期待的是完全陌生的东西、另一个天才、另一个世界。
这些是呼喊，在呼喊里他满怀激情地立刻离开对美德的庸常估价，满怀激情地宣告另一种权利和光明、生命的另一个领域，而后者与世界的关系只能是：被世界仇恨和迫害。
但在这个上帝之国里，他向他们指出的不是法律的消解，而是法律必须由一种正义来充实，这种正义是另一种正义，其中含有更多的东西，比那些义务人的正义更完整：是对法律缺陷的一种补足。

en: He then shows this filling-up on several laws; one can call this containing-more-in-itself a inclination to act as the laws would command106), a unity of the inclination with the law, whereby the latter loses its form as law; this agreement of the inclination is the πλήϱωμα of the law, a being that, as one otherwise expressed it, is the complement of possibility; for possibility is the object as something thought, the universal; being [is] the synthesis of subject and object, in which subject and object have lost their opposition; likewise that inclination, a virtue, is a synthesis in which the law (which Kant therefore always calls an objective one) loses its universality and likewise the subject its particularity, — both lose their opposition; whereas in the Kantian virtue this opposition remains and the one becomes the ruling, the other the ruled.

The agreement of the inclination with the law is of such a kind that law and inclination are no longer different; and the expression agreement of the inclination with the law becomes therefore wholly unsuitable, because in it law and inclination still occur as particular, as opposed, and could easily be understood as a support of the moral disposition, of respect for [the] law and of the determination of the will by the law — through the inclination different from it; and since the agreeing ones are different, the agreement too would be only accidental, only the unity of something foreign, something thought.

But since here in the complement of the laws (and what is connected with it) duty, moral disposition and the like cease to be something universal [opposed] to the inclination, and the inclination ceases to be something particular opposed to the law, that agreement is life and, as the relation of different ones, love, a being that, expressed as concept, as law, is necessarily equal to the law, i.e. to itself, or, as actual, as inclination, opposed to the concept, is likewise equal to itself, to the inclination.107)
zh: 接着他在若干法律上指出这种充实的东西；人们可以把这种自身含有更多东西的状态称为一种这样去行动的倾向，即像法律所命令的那样去行动106)，称为偏好与法律的统一，法律由此失去它作为法律的形式；这种偏好的符合就是法律的πλήϱωμα，是一种存在，按人们从前的说法，就是可能性的补充；因为可能性是客体，作为被思想的东西，即普遍的东西；存在则是主体与客体的综合，在其中有主体和客体失去了它们的对立；同样，那种倾向、一种美德，也是一种综合，在其中有法律（康德因此总把它称为客观的）失去它的普遍性，主体也同样失去它的特殊性，——两者都失去它们的对立；与此相反，在康德式的美德里这种对立保留着，一方成为统治的，另一方成为被统治的。
偏好与法律的符合是这样一个符合，以致法律和偏好不再有区别；而“偏好与法律的符合”这个说法因此变得完全不恰当，因为在它里面法律和偏好还作为特殊的东西、作为对立的东西出现，而且很容易被理解为对道德意向、对法律的敬重以及意志由法律来规定的一种支持——靠那种与法律不同的偏好来支持；又因为相符合的双方是有区别的，这种符合也就只能是偶然的，只能是陌生东西的统一、一种被思想的东西。
但既然在这里，在法律的补充中（以及与此相关的东西中），义务、道德意向之类不再是[与偏好]对立的普遍的东西，偏好也不再是与法律对立的特殊的东西，那么这种符合就是生命，而作为有区别者的关系就是爱，是一种存在，它作为概念、作为法律表达出来，必然与法律、也就是与自身相同，或者作为现实的东西、作为偏好，与概念相对立，同样与自身、与偏好相同。107)

en: Thus the commandment: thou shalt not kill, is a principle that is recognized as valid for the will of every rational being, that can count as the principle of a universal legislation.

Jesus sets over against such a commandment the higher genius of conciliatoriness (a modification of love), which not only does not act against that law, but makes it quite superfluous, contains in itself so much richer living fullness that for it such a paltry thing as such a law does not exist at all.

What conciliatoriness lacks in the universality that in the concept comprehends all the particular within itself, since in it the law loses its form, the concept of life is displaced, is only an apparent loss and a true infinite gain through the richness of living relations with the perhaps few individuals with whom it enters into relation.

It excludes not actual things but thought things, possibilities, and this richness of possibility in the universality of the concept, the form of the commandment, is itself a tearing-apart of life and as to its content so paltry that, apart from the single maltreatment forbidden in it, it permits all the rest; before conciliatoriness, by contrast, anger too is a crime, and [likewise] the quick reaction of the feeling of an oppression, the surging up to oppress again, which is a kind of blind justice and thus indeed presupposes equality, but of enemies; [while] the spirit of conciliatoriness, by contrast, is in itself without hostile disposition, strives to sublate the other's enmity.

If one judges according to love, then it is also, and indeed a greater crime than anger, to scold one's brother as a scoundrel; but a scoundrel in his isolating, in which he sets himself, a human being, hostilely over against the human being and strives to persist in this derangement, is still held for something, he still counts, for he is hated, and a great scoundrel can be admired; to love it is therefore still more alien to declare the other a fool, which sublates not only all relation with him but also all equality, all community of essence, utterly subjugates him in representation, designates him as a nothing.108)
zh: 所以，诫命「你不可杀人」是一条原则，它被认识到对每一个理性存在者的意志都有效，可以作为一条普遍立法的原则。
耶稣拿更高的和解天才（爱的一种变形）来与这样的诫命相对，这种和解天才不仅不违背那条法律，反而让它完全成了多余的，它自身包含着如此更丰富的、活生生的充实，以至于对它来说，像这样一条法律那样贫乏的东西根本不存在。
和解天才在那种普遍性——即在概念里把一切特殊的东西都包含在自身的普遍性——上所缺少的东西，因为在它里面法律失去了自己的形式，生命的概念被挤掉了，这只是一个表面上的损失，而通过它与也许少数几个个体之间活生生的关系的丰富，它与这些个体发生关系，却是一个真实的、无限的收获。

它排除的不是现实的东西，而是被思考的东西、可能性，而这种在概念的普遍性里的可能性的丰富，即诫命的形式，本身就是对生命的一种撕裂，而且按其内容来说是如此贫乏，以至于除了它里面唯一禁止的那种虐待之外，它允许其余一切；而在和解天才面前，愤怒也是一种罪行，同样，感到被压制时那种迅速的反应，即反过来再压制别人的那股火，也是一种罪行，这股火是一种盲目的公正，因此毕竟还预设了平等，但预设的是敌对者之间的平等；而和解的精神自身则没有敌对的意向，它力求扬弃别人的敌意。

如果按爱来判断，那么骂自己的兄弟是恶棍，对爱来说也是一桩罪行，而且是一桩比愤怒更大的罪行；但一个恶棍在他那种孤立中——在这种孤立里，他把自己这个人敌对地放到人面前，并且力求在这种错乱中维持下去——还算是点东西，还有分量，因为他被恨，而一个大恶棍甚至可以被钦佩；所以对爱来说，把别人说成傻瓜就更加陌生，这样做不仅扬弃了与他的全部关系，而且扬弃了全部平等、全部本质上的共同性，在表象中把他彻底压服，把他指为一个无。108)

en: By contrast, love, which before the altar becomes conscious of a disunion, leaves its sacrifice there, reconciles itself with the brother, and only then steps pure and united before the unifying deity.
It does not let the judge measure out its right to it, but reconciles itself without any regard for right.109)
zh: 与此相反，爱如果在祭坛前意识到一种分裂，就把自己的献祭留在那里，与兄弟和解，然后才纯净地、合一地走到那唯一的神面前。
它不让法官给它量出它的权利，而是不顾一切权利地和解。109)

en: In the same way Jesus sets love over against the dutiful fidelity in marriage and the right to divorce oneself from the wife, [love] which also excludes the desire that that duty did not forbid, and sublates this permission, which was contradictory to that duty, with one exception.

Thus on the one hand the holiness of love is the completion (the πλήϱωμα) of the law against adultery; and this holiness alone gives the capacity, if one of the many sides of the human being wanted to raise itself to the whole or against the whole, to hold it down, and only the feeling of the whole, love, is able to prevent the dispersal of the essence — on the other hand love sublates the permission to divorce; and against love there can be no talk of permission and right, neither as long as it lives nor as it ceases.

The ceasing of love toward a wife in whom love still is makes it become unfaithful to itself and sin; and a transfer of its passion is only a straying of the same, which it must atone for with a bad conscience.

Its fate, to be sure, cannot be spared it in this case, and the marriage is in itself separated, but the assistance that the man fetches from a right and a law, and through which he draws legality and propriety onto his side, means adding to the violation of the wife's love yet a base harshness.
Only in the case that Jesus excepts, when the wife has turned her love to another, can the man not remain her servant.
To the Jews, σϰληϱοι ͂ς ϰαϱδίᾳ, Moses indeed had to give laws and rights about marriage; but from the beginning it was not so.
zh: 同样，耶稣拿爱来与婚姻中合乎义务的忠诚和与妻子离婚的权利相对，爱把那种义务并未禁止的情欲也排除掉，并且把这种与那种义务相矛盾的许可，除了一个例外，都扬弃了。
所以，一方面，爱的神圣性是那条禁止通奸的法律的补足（πλήϱωμα）；唯有这种神圣性才给出能力，当人身上许多方面中的一个方面想要把自己提升到整体、或者起来反对整体时，把它压住，而且只有对整体的感受，即爱，才能阻止本质的涣散——另一方面，爱扬弃了离婚的许可；而在爱面前，无论它活着的时候还是它停止的时候，都谈不上许可和权利。
对还怀着爱的妻子不再有爱，这就使爱自己变得不忠、犯下罪；而把它的激情转移到别处，只是它的一次迷误，它必须怀着内疚去赎。
在这种情况下，爱的命运当然免不了，婚姻自在地就已经分离了，但男人从一种权利和一种法律那里搬来的援助，以及他借此把循规蹈矩和体面拉到自己这一边，这就叫作给对妻子的爱的伤害再添上一种卑鄙的严厉。
只有在耶稣所除外的那个情况下——妻子已经把她的爱转向了别人——男人才可以不再做她的奴仆。
对犹太人，σϰληϱοι ͂ς ϰαϱδίᾳ〔心硬的人〕，摩西只好就婚姻给出法律和权利；但从起初并不是这样。

en: In an assurance about something actual, the subject and the object are thought as separated, or in an assurance about something future, in a promise, the declaration of a will and the deed itself still [as] wholly separated; and it is a matter of the truth, i.e. of the firm connection of the two; in an oath-bound assurance, the representation of the deed either already happened or only future is tied to something divine, the connection of the word and the deed, the linkage, being itself is presented on a being, made present in it, and because the truth of the case that is sworn to cannot itself be made visible, in its place the truth itself, God, is posited and is partly in this way given to the other, produces conviction in him, partly through the reaction of this being upon the resolving mind of the swearer the opposite of the truth is excluded; and it is not at all to be seen how a superstition is supposed to lie in this.

If the Jews swore by heaven, by earth, by Jerusalem or by their hair, and left their oath to God, laid it into the hand of the Lord, then they tied the actuality of what was assured to an object, set both actualities equal, and the connection of this object and of the assured thing, the equality of both, they laid into the power of a foreign might, and God is posited as the might over the word, and this connection is supposed to be grounded in the human being himself; the assured deed and the object by which the assurance is made are so chained to one another that, if the one is sublated, the other too is denied, is sublated in representation; if therefore the promised deed or the assured actuality is not actual, then with it the object by which the oath was sworn, heaven, earth, etc., is also denied; and in this case the lord of the same must vindicate it, God must become the avenger of what is his. — It is this tying of the assured deed to something objective that Jesus contradicts, he does not confirm the duty of keeping the oath, but declares it superfluous altogether; for neither heaven, nor earth, nor Jerusalem, nor the hair is the human being's spirit, which alone is the linker of his word and an action, but [they] are foreign property, and the certainty of the deed may not be tied to something foreign, be laid into something foreign, but the connection of the word and the action must be living, must rest in the human being himself.
zh: 在对一件现实事情的保证里，主体和客体被思考为分离的，或者在对一件将来的事情的保证里，在一个承诺里，一个意志的宣布和那行为本身还〔被思考为〕完全分离的；这里要紧的是真，即两者的牢固关联；在一种起誓的保证里，那件或者已经发生、或者还只在将来的行为的表象被系在某种神圣的东西上，话语和行为的关联、这种联结、存在本身，被在一个存在者身上表现出来，在它里面被当前化，而因为所起誓的那件事的真本身不能被弄成可见的，所以就以真本身、以上帝来代替它，并且一部分以这种方式把它交给别人，在别人心里造成确信，另一部分则通过这个存在者反过来作用于起誓者那正在下决心的心志，把真的反面排除掉；至于这里面怎么会有一种迷信，那根本是看不出来的。

如果犹太人对天、对地、对耶路撒冷、或者对自己的头发起誓，把自己的誓言交给上帝，把它放到主的手里，那么他们就是把自己所保证的东西的现实性系在一个客体上，把两种现实性设为相等，并且把这个客体与所保证的东西之间的关联、把两者的相等，放到一种异己力量的支配之下，于是上帝就被设为支配话语的力量，而这种关联本应奠立在人自己身上；所保证的行为和用来起誓的客体被这样彼此锁在一起，以至于一个被扬弃，另一个也就被否定、在表象中被扬弃；所以，如果所承诺的行为或所保证的现实性并不现实，那么用来起誓的客体，天、地等等，也就随之被否定了；在这种情况下，它的主人就必须索回它，上帝就必须成为他自己的东西的报复者——耶稣反对的正是这种把所保证的行为系在某种客观东西上的做法，他并不是在确认守誓的义务，而是干脆宣布誓言是多余的；因为无论天、地、耶路撒冷还是头发，都不是人的精神，只有人的精神才是把他的话语和一个行为联结起来的东西，那些都是异己的财产，行为的确定性不可以系在某种异己的东西上、被放进某种异己的东西里，而话语和行为的关联必须是活的，必须建立在人自己身上。

en: An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, say the laws; retaliation and the equality of the same is the holy principle of all justice, the principle on which every state constitution must rest.

But Jesus demands in general a giving up of right, an elevation above the whole sphere of justice or injustice through love, in which, along with right, this feeling of inequality too and the ought of this feeling, which demands equality, i.e. the hatred of enemies, disappears.
zh: 以眼还眼，以牙还牙，法律这样说；报复以及报复的平等，是一切公正的神圣原则，是每一种国家宪法都必须立足于其上的原则。
但耶稣一般地要求放弃权利，要求通过爱把自己提升到公正或不公正的整个领域之上，在爱里面，随着权利一起，这种不平等的感受以及这种感受所要求的应当，即对敌人的恨，也都消失了。

en: The laws and duties of which Jesus has so far spoken were on the whole civil ones, and the completion that he gave them was not that he confirmed them as laws and duties but demanded pure respect for them as motive, but rather shows contempt for them, and his completion is a spirit whose actions, if they are judged according to laws and commandments of duty, are found to accord with them, but which has no consciousness for duties and rights.

Further he speaks of a merely moral duty, the virtue of beneficence; in its case, as with prayer and fasting, Jesus condemns the mixing in of something foreign, the impurity of the action; he does it not in order to be seen —: the purpose of the action, i.e. the action as thought, before it is still done, is to be equal to the completed action.

Besides this hypocrisy, which mixes into the thought of the action the other thing, being seen by human beings, which is not in the action, Jesus here too seems himself to remove the consciousness of the action as a fulfilled duty.

「Let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth」 cannot be taken as about the action's becoming known, but is the opposite of: being seen by people, and if it is therefore to have a sense, it will designate one's own reflection upon one's dutifulness.
Whether in the action only I, or whether I think that others too are watching me, whether I enjoy only my consciousness or also the approval of others, is surely no great difference.

For the recognized approval of others over a victory that duty, the universal, has carried off over the particular, is as it were no longer merely the thought but the intuited universality and particularity, the former in the representation of the others, the latter in the others as actual ones themselves; and the lonely consciousness of the fulfilled duty is different from honor not in kind, but only insofar as in honor the universality is recognized not merely as universally valid but also as universally holding; in one's own consciousness of having fulfilled the duty, the individual himself gives himself the character of universality, he intuits himself as a universal, as exalted above himself as particular and above what lies in the concept of particularity, above the multitude of individuals; for just as the concept of universality is applied to the individual, so the concept of particularity also receives this relation to individuals and their opposition of the same to that which itself knows itself according to the universal, in fulfillment of duty; and this self-consciousness is just as foreign to the action as the approval of human beings.

Of this conviction of being righteous in oneself, and of the putting-down of others thereby (both of which stand in necessary connection, because of the necessary opposition of the particular to the universal), Jesus also speaks in the parable Luk.

The Pharisee thanks God for it, he is so modest as not to recognize the strength of his will in it, that he is not like many other human beings, who are robbers, unjust, adulterers, or like the tax collector here beside him; he fasts according to the rule and as an upright man conscientiously pays his tithe.

Over against this consciousness of uprightness, of which it is not at all said that it was not true, Jesus sets the downcast gaze of the tax collector, which does not dare to raise itself to heaven, who beats his breast: God be gracious to me, a sinner.
The consciousness of the Pharisee of having fulfilled his duty, as also the consciousness of the young man of having been a faithful observer of all laws (Matth.

19, 20), this good conscience is therefore a hypocrisy because it is partly, when it is indeed connected with the intention of the action, a reflection upon itself, upon the action, something impure, not belonging to the action, partly, when it is a representation of oneself as a moral human being, [as] it presents itself in the Pharisee and in that young man, [it is] a representation whose content is the virtues, i.e. limited things, to which their circle is given, [which] are bounded in their material, thus all together are something incomplete, since the good conscience, the consciousness of having fulfilled one's duties, hypocritically feigns itself to be the whole.
zh: 耶稣到此为止所说的法律和义务，大体上是市民的，他给它们添上的补足，并不是他把它们确认为法律和义务、却要求把它们当作动力来纯粹敬重，而是恰恰表现出对它们的蔑视，他的补足是一种精神，这种精神的行动如果按法律和义务诫命来评判，会被发现是合乎这些法律和义务诫命的，但这种精神对义务和权利没有意识。
接下来他谈到一种纯然道德的义务，即行善这一美德；在这里，像在祷告和禁食时一样，耶稣谴责的是掺进某种异己的东西、是行为的不纯；他这样做不是为了被人看见——：行为的目的，也就是行为在被做出之前作为被思考的行为，等于已经完成的行为。
除了这种伪善——它在行为的思想里掺进那种并不在行为里的别的东西，即被人看见——耶稣在这里似乎自己也把行为作为已履行义务的意识去掉。
「不要让你的左手知道你右手所做的」，不能理解为行为被人知道，而是与「被人看见」相反，所以，如果它要有一种意思的话，那它指的就是自己对自己的合乎义务性所作的反思。
在行为中，是只有我，还是我想到别人也在看着我，是我只享受自己的意识，还是也享受别人的赞同，这大概不是什么大的区别。

因为别人对义务、对普遍的东西战胜特殊的东西所取得的胜利表示赞同，这种被认识到的赞同，可以说已经不再只是被思考的普遍性和特殊性，而是被直观到的普遍性和特殊性，前者在别人的表象里，后者在作为现实者的别人自己身上；而已履行义务的那种孤独的意识，与荣誉的区别不在于种类，而只在于：在荣誉里，普遍性不仅被认识到是普遍有效的，而且被认识到是普遍地有效的；在自己已经履行义务的意识里，个体自己给自己加上了普遍性的品格，他把自己直观为一个普遍的东西，直观为高出作为特殊的自己、高出一切包含在特殊性概念里的东西、高出众多个人；因为正如普遍性的概念被用在个体身上，特殊性的概念也同样获得这种对个人的关系，以及这些个人与那个按照普遍的东西、在履行义务中认识自己的东西相对立；而这种自我意识对行为来说，正如人的赞同一样是异己的。
关于这种自己在自己面前是公正的确信，以及由此对他人的贬低（这两者必然联系在一起，因为特殊的东西必然与普遍的东西相对立），耶稣在 Luk. 的比喻里也谈到了。
那个法利赛人为这事感谢上帝，他如此谦卑，竟不认为这是他自己意志的力量：他不像许多别的人那样是强盗、不义的人、通奸的人，也不像他旁边这个税吏；他按规定禁食，并且作为一个正直的人认真地缴纳他的十分之一。
对这种正直的意识——并没有说它不是真的——耶稣拿那个税吏低垂的、不敢向天抬起的目光来与它相对，那税吏捶着自己的胸口：上帝啊，开恩可怜我这个罪人。
法利赛人那种自己已经履行了义务的意识，以及那个青年那种自己一向是全部法律的一个忠实遵守者的意识（Matth.

19, 20），这种好的良心之所以是一种伪善，是因为：一方面，当它已经与行为的意图结合在一起时，它是一种对自己、对行为的反思，是一种不纯的、并不属于行为的东西；另一方面，当它是把自己作为一个道德的人的表象时——就像在法利赛人和那个青年身上所表现的那样——它就是一个表象，其内容是一些美德，也就是一些有限制的东西，它们各有自己被给予的范围，在自己的材料上受到限制，所以合在一起是一个不完整的东西，因为好的良心、已经履行了自己的各种义务的意识，把自己伪装成了整体。

en: In this very spirit Jesus speaks of praying and fasting; both are either wholly objective, strictly commanded duties or grounded only in a need; they are not capable of being represented as moral duties, because they presuppose no opposition that would be capable of being united in a concept; in both Jesus censures the show that one gives oneself before men by it, and in prayer especially also the much chattering, whereby it gets the appearance of a duty and of the exercise of the same.
Fasting Jesus judges (Matth.
9, 15) according to the feeling that lies at its basis, according to the need that drives to it.
Besides the removal of uncleanness in prayer, Jesus also indicates a way of praying; the consideration of what is true in prayer does not belong in this place.
zh: 正是在这同一种精神里，耶稣谈到祈祷和禁食；这两样要么是完全客观的、绝对被命令的义务，要么只是建立在一个需要之上；它们不能被表象为道德义务，因为它们并不预设一种能够在某个概念里被结合起来的对立；对这两样，耶稣都责备人在人前借此做出来的假象，对祈祷还特别责备那种喋喋不休，它由此得到一种义务和履行义务的外观。
禁食，耶稣评判它（Matth.
9, 15）按它底下所依据的感受，按驱使人去做的需要。
除了在祈祷中除去不洁，耶稣还指出一种祈祷的方式；对祈祷里什么是真的这一考虑，不属于这个地方。

en: About the following demand to cast off the cares of life and to despise riches, as well as about Matth.

19, 23: how hard it is for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God, there is probably nothing to say; it is a litany that is only indulged in sermons or in rhymes, for such a demand has no truth for us.
The fate of property has become too powerful for us for reflections about it to be bearable, for its separation from us to be thinkable for us.

But this much is at least to be seen, that the possession of wealth, with all the rights as well as with all the cares that hang together with it, brings determinacies into men, whose limits set the virtues their boundary, assign them conditions and dependencies, within which there is indeed room for duties and virtues, but which allow no whole, no complete life, because it is bound to objects, has conditions of itself outside itself, because to life something is still conceded as its own that yet can never be its property.

Wealth immediately betrays its opposition to love, to wholeness, by the fact that it is a right and is comprehended in a manifoldness of rights, whereby partly the virtue that relates immediately to it, uprightness, partly the other virtues possible within its circle are necessarily bound up with exclusion, and every act of virtue is in itself an opposite.
Of a syncretism, a service of two lords, there is no thinking, because the indeterminate and the determinate cannot be united while retaining their forms.
Jesus had to point out not merely the complement of the duties but also the object of these principles, the essence of the sphere of duties, in order to destroy the domain opposed to love.
zh: 关于下面这个抛弃生活之忧、鄙视财富的要求，以及关于 Matth.
19, 23：财主进上帝之国是何等难，这大概没什么可说的；这是一段连祷文，只有在讲道词或韵文里才被将就着念过去，因为这样一种要求对我们没有真理。
财产的命运对我们来说已经变得太强大，以致对它的反思难以忍受，它同我们的分离对我们来说无法设想。
但至少可以看出这一点：拥有财富，连同与它相关的一切权利和一切忧虑，会给人带来一些规定性，这些规定性的界限为各种美德划出边界，给它们指出条件和依赖，在这些条件和依赖之内固然有义务和美德的余地，但它们不允许一个整体、一种完整的生命，因为生命被束缚在对象上，它的条件在它自身之外，因为还有某种东西被承认为生命自己的，而那东西永远不能成为它的财产。
财富马上就暴露出它对爱、对整体性的对立，因为它是一种权利，并且被包含在权利的杂多之中，由此，一方面那直接与它相关的美德、即正直，另一方面在它的圈子之内可能有的其他美德，都必然和排斥连在一起，而每一个美德行为自在就是某种与之对立的东西。
谈不上什么混合主义、两个主人的侍奉，因为不确定的东西和确定的东西在保持各自形式的情况下无法结合起来。
耶稣不只要指出义务的补足，还要指出这些原则的对象、义务领域的本质，才能摧毁那个与爱相对立的领域。

en: Luke (12, 13) presents the view according to which Jesus declares himself against riches in a connection, whereby it becomes still clearer.

A man had addressed him with the request to intercede with his brother about the division of their inheritance; to decline a request for such an intercession is judged to be only the procedure of an egoist.
Jesus seems in his answer to hold up against the one who had made the request to him immediately only his incompetence for it.

But in his spirit there lies more than that he merely has no right to that division, for he turns at once to his disciples with an admonition against the desire to have, and adds a parable of a rich man whom God startles with the voice: "Fool! this night your soul will be demanded of you — what you have acquired, whose will it be?
So it is with him who gathers treasures for himself and is not rich in God."

Thus Jesus turns the side of right only to that profane man, while against his disciples he demands elevation above the domain of right, of justice, of equity, of the services of friendship, which men in this domain can render one another, above the whole sphere of property.
zh: 路加（12, 13）把耶稣反对财富所依据的那种看法放在一个联系里讲出来，它由此变得更清楚。
一个人曾为此求他，要他去向那人的兄弟说情，分割他们的遗产；拒绝这样一个说情的请求，会被看成只是一个利己主义者的做法。
耶稣在回答里，对那个向他提出请求的人，似乎只是直截了当地拿自己对此没有资格来顶回去。
但在他精神里还有更多的东西，不只是他对那种分割没有权利，因为他马上转向他的门徒，告诫他们不要有想占有的贪欲，还附上一个比喻，讲一个财主，上帝用声音把他惊醒：“无知的人！今夜就要你的灵魂——你所积攒的，要归谁呢？
凡为自己积攒财宝、在上帝那里不富足的，就是这样。”
所以耶稣只对那个世俗的人讲权利这一面，而对门徒，他要求他们超出权利、正义、公道和朋友间互助的领域——这些是人在这个领域里能彼此做到的——超出整个财产的领域。

en: To conscience, the consciousness of one's own conformity or non-conformity to duty, there stands opposed the application of the laws to others in judgment; "judge not," says Jesus, "that you be not judged; with what measure you measure, it will be measured to you in return".

This subsuming of others under a concept that is represented in the law can therefore be called a weakness, because the one who judges is not strong enough to bear them wholly, but divides them, and cannot hold out against their independence, [takes] them not as they are but as they ought to be; through which judgment he has subjugated them to himself in thought, for the concept, the universality, is his.

But with this judging he has acknowledged a law and subjected himself to slavery under it, set up a measure of judging also for himself, and with the loving disposition toward his brother, to pull the splinter out of his eye, he himself has sunk below the realm of love.
zh: 与良心、与对自己合乎义务或不合义务的意识相对的，是在判断中把法律用到别人身上；“你们不要判断”，耶稣说，“免得你们被判断；你们用什么尺度量，也就要用什么尺度量给你们。”
把别人归到一个在法律里被表述出来的概念之下，这之所以可以叫作一种软弱，是因为作判断的人不够强，不能把他们整个承受下来，而是把他们分开，面对他们的独立性撑不住，不是把他们当作本来的样子，而是当作他们应当的样子；通过这个判断，他在思想上把他们制伏了，因为概念、普遍性是他的。
可是凭着这种判断，他承认了一条法律，让自己受了它的奴役，也为自己立了一个判断的尺度；而带着对兄弟的慈爱意向，要把他眼里的刺挑出来，他自己却已经沉到爱的领域之下去了。

en: What follows further is no longer an opposition of that which is higher than the laws to them, but the pointing out of some expressions of life in its beautiful free region, as the union of men in asking, giving and receiving.

The whole closes with the effort to present the image of man purely outside this sphere, as he is sketched in the preceding in opposition to the determinacies, which is why the pure also appeared more in its modifications, in particular virtues such as conciliatoriness, marital fidelity, truthfulness, etc., which of course can only happen in incomplete parables.
zh: 后面接着讲的，不再是拿高于法律的东西来与法律对立，而是指出生命在它那美好自由的领域里的几种表现，即人在请求、给予和接受中的结合。
整个结尾的努力，是要把人的形象纯粹地放到这个领域之外来呈现——这个形象在前面是当作与各种规定性相对立的东西来勾画的，因此纯粹的东西也更多是在它的各种变样中、在和解、夫妇忠诚、真诚等等特殊美德中出现——而这当然只能在不完整的比喻里做到。

en: A contrast with this lawlessness and dutylessness in love, which Jesus designates as the highest, is made by the manner of John the Baptist, of which Luke (Kap. 3) has preserved some samples.
How they could still hope, although they have Abraham as father, he says to the Jews, to escape their angered fate: "The axe is already laid at the root of the trees."

And since the Jews then asked him what they were to do, he said, whoever has two coats or superfluous food, let him give it to him who has not; the tax collectors he admonished to demand no more dues than are prescribed for them; the soldiers, to plague no one, to extort nothing, but to live from their pay; further it is known of him (Matth.

14, 4), that he entered into abuse over Herod's relation with his brother's wife; a scolding that cost him his head; his fate was fulfilled over a determinacy; as his teaching, according to the samples above, was an admonition to determinate virtues, and does not show in his consciousness the great spirit, the all-embracing soul of them.

He felt this himself too and announced another who, with the winnowing shovel in his hand, will sweep the threshing floor; John hopes in faith, instead of his water baptism, for a baptism with fire and spirit from his successor.
zh: 与这种在爱里没有法律、没有义务的状态——耶稣把它称为最高的——形成对照的，是施洗约翰的做法，路加（Kap. 3）为它保存了几个样品。
他们虽然以亚伯拉罕为父，却还怎么能指望逃脱自己那被激怒的命运，他对犹太人说：“斧子已经放在树根上了。”
犹太人问他该做什么，他就说，谁有两件衣服或有富余的食物，就把它给那没有的人；他告诫税吏，不要索取超过规定给他们征收的税；告诫士兵，不要欺负人，不要勒索，而要靠着他们的军饷过活；关于他还有一件事为人所知（Matth.
14, 4），就是他卷入对希律与他兄弟的妻子的关系的辱骂；这一顿斥责让他丢了脑袋；他的命运是在一个规定性上完成的；正如他的教导按上面几个样品来看，是对各种确定美德的劝诫，却没有在他的意识里显出那种伟大的精神，那种把这一切都包揽在内的灵魂。
他自己也感觉到这一点，并且宣告了另一个人，那人手里拿着扬场锨，要清扫打谷场；约翰在信心里希望从自己的后继者那里得到一种以火与精神的洗礼，来代替他自己的水洗。

en: To the positivity of the Jews Jesus opposed man, to the laws and their duties the virtues, and in these he sublated the immorality of the positive man.

The positive man is indeed, with regard to a determinate virtue that is service for him and in him, neither moral nor immoral, and the service in which he exercises certain duties is not immediately a vice against those same duties, but with this determinate indifference an immorality from another side is at the same time linked; because his determinate positive service has a limit and he cannot go beyond it, he is immoral beyond it.

This immorality of positivity therefore bears upon a different side of human relations than positive obedience does — within its own circle, the non-moral is not the immoral.110) In the positing of subjectivity against the positive, the indifference of service and its limit vanish.
Man stands on his own, his character and his deed become he himself; he has limits only where he himself posits them, and his virtues are determinacies that he himself delimits.
This possibility of limiting the opposition is freedom, the “or” in virtue or vice.

In the opposition of the law to nature, of the universal to the particular, both opposites are posited, actual, the one is not without the other; in the moral freedom of the opposition of virtue and vice, the other is excluded by the one, so that if the one is posited, the other is only possible.
The opposition of duty and inclination has found its union in the modifications of love, in the virtues.

Since the law was opposed to love not according to its content but according to its form, it could be taken up into love, but in this taking up it lost its shape; to crime, on the other hand, it is opposed according to its content; it is excluded by crime, and yet it is; for crime is a destruction of nature; and since nature is one, as much is destroyed in the destroyer as in the destroyed.

If the unified is opposed, then the union of the opposites is present only in the concept, a law has been made; if the opposite has been destroyed, then the concept, the law, remains; but it then expresses only what is missing, a gap, because its content is sublated in actuality, and it is called punitive law.

This form of the law is immediate, it is opposed to life according to its content, because it indicates the destruction of life; but it is all the harder to think how the law in this form, as punitive justice, could be sublated; in the previous sublation of the law through the virtues, only the form of the law disappeared, its content remained; but here, with the form, its content too would be sublated, for its content is punishment.
zh: 对于犹太人的实证性，耶稣把人置于其对立面，对于法律及其义务则把美德置于其对立面，并且在这些美德中扬弃了实证的人的不道德。
实证的人就一种特定的美德而言——这种美德对他是服务，在他身上也是服务——既不是道德的，也不是不道德的，而他在其中履行某些义务的那种服务，并不直接就是针对这些义务的一种恶德；但与这种特定的无差别连在一起的，同时还有从另一面来的不道德；因为他那种特定的实证服务有一个界限，他无法越过它，所以一越过这个界限，他就是不道德的。
所以实证性的这种不道德，落在人际关系中与实证的服从不同的另一面上——在它自己的圈子里，非道德并不是不道德。110）在主体性被设定为与实证的东西对立时，服务的无差别和它的界限就消失了。
人是自立的，他的性格和他的行为变成他自己；他只在自身设定限制的地方才有种种限制，而他的美德是他自己加以限定的种种规定性。
这种限制对立的可能性就是自由，就是美德或恶行中的那个“或”。
在法律与自然相对立、普遍者与特殊者相对立时，两个对立者都是被设定的、现实的，一个离了另一个就不存在；而在美德与恶行相对立的道德自由中，一个把另一个排除掉了，所以一个被设定时，另一个只是可能的。
义务与偏好的对立，在爱的种种变式中、在美德中找到了它们的结合。
法律与爱相对立，不是按它的内容，而是按它的形式，所以它可以被接纳进爱之中，但在这种接纳中它失去了自己的形态；而它与罪行则是按内容相对立的；它被罪行排除在外，却仍然存在；因为罪行是对自然的摧毁；而既然自然是一体的，那么在破坏者那里被摧毁的，就和在被摧毁者那里被摧毁的一样多。
如果一体的东西被对立起来，那么对立双方的结合就只存在于概念中，于是就造成了一条法律；如果对立的一方被摧毁了，那么概念、法律仍然留着；但它这时表达的只是缺失的东西，一个缺口，因为它的内容在现实性中已被扬弃，于是它就叫惩罚的法律。
法律的这种形式是直接的，它按其内容与生命相对立，因为它标示的是对生命的摧毁；但正因如此，要设想法律在这种形式中、作为惩罚的正义如何能被扬弃，就显得越发困难；在先前通过美德对法律的扬弃中，消失的只是法律的形式，它的内容留了下来；但在这里，随形式一起被扬弃的还有它的内容，因为它的内容就是惩罚。

en: Punishment lies immediately in the offended law; of the same right that has been violated in another by a crime, the criminal is deprived.111)
The criminal has posited himself outside the concept that is the content of the law.

True, the law only says that he shall lose the right comprehended in the law; but because it is immediately only something thought, only the concept of the criminal loses the right; and in order that he lose it in actuality, i.e. that what the concept of the criminal has lost should also be lost by the actuality of the criminal, the law must be joined with something living, clothed with power.

Now although the law persists in its terrible majesty — and that the punishment of the crime is deserved, this indeed can never be sublated; the law cannot give the punishment away, cannot be gracious, for it would sublate itself; the law has been broken by the criminal, its content is no longer for him, he has sublated it; but the form of the law, universality, pursues him and even clings to his crime; his deed becomes universal, and the right that he has sublated is sublated for him too.

So the law remains, and the deserving of a punishment remains; but the living being whose power has united itself with the law, the executor who takes from the criminal in actuality the right lost in the concept, the judge, is not abstract justice, but a being, and justice only its modification.

The necessity of deserving the punishment is fixed, but the exercise of justice is nothing necessary, because as the modification of a living being it can also pass away, another modification can enter; and so justice becomes something contingent; there can be a contradiction between it as universal, thought, and it as actual, i.e. as existing in a living being; an avenger can forgive, can give up revenging himself; a judge [can cease] to act as judge, can pardon.

But justice is not thereby satisfied; it is unbending, and as long as laws are the highest, so long can it not be escaped, so long must the individual be sacrificed to the universal, i.e. it must be killed.

Therefore it is also contradictory to think that the law could be satisfied in one representative of many equal criminals; for insofar as in him the others too should undergo the punishment, he is the universal, the concept of them, and the law, as commanding or as punishing, is law only by being opposed to something particular.

The law has the condition of its universality in this, that the acting men or the actions are particular; and the actions are particular insofar as they are considered in relation to universality, to the laws, as in accordance with them or contrary to them; and insofar their relation, their determinacy, can suffer no change; they are actual, they are what they are; what has happened cannot be made unhappened, punishment follows the deed; their connection is indissoluble; if there is no way to make an action unhappened, if its actuality is eternal, then no reconciliation is possible, not even through undergoing the punishment; the law is indeed satisfied thereby, for the contradiction between its pronounced ought and the actuality of the criminal, the exception that the criminal wanted to make from universality, is sublated.

But the criminal is not reconciled with the law (let this be for the criminal a foreign being or subjectively in him, as bad conscience); in the former case, the foreign power that the criminal has created and armed against himself, this hostile being, ceases, once it has punished, to act upon him; when it has reacted upon him in just the way in which the criminal acted, it indeed desists, but withdraws into the threatening posture, and its shape has not vanished or been made friendly; on bad conscience, the consciousness of a bad action, of oneself as bad, the punishment suffered changes nothing; for the criminal always beholds himself as criminal, he has no power over his action as an actuality, and this his actuality is in contradiction with his consciousness of the law.
zh: 惩罚直接就存在于被冒犯的法律之中；罪犯因一桩罪行在别人身上所侵害的同一权利，他自己也丧失了。111）
罪犯把自己设定到了那个作为法律内容的概念之外。
法律固然只是说，他应当失去法律所包含的权利；但因为它直接地只是一个被思想的东西，所以失去权利的只是罪犯的概念；而要他在现实性中也失去它，也就是说，要让罪犯的概念所失去的东西也由罪犯的现实性失去，法律就必须与活的东西相结合，必须披上权力。
法律固然在其可怕的威严中持续着——罪行的惩罚是应得的，这一点永远不能被扬弃；法律不能把惩罚赠送出去，不能开恩，因为那它就扬弃了自己；法律已被罪犯破坏，它的内容对他来说不再存在，他已经把它扬弃了；但法律的形式、即普遍性，却追着他，甚至贴附到他的罪行上；他的行为变成普遍的，而他所扬弃的权利，对他来说也被扬弃了。
所以法律留着，应受惩罚这一点也留着；但那个其权力已与法律结合起来的活的东西，那个在现实性中把概念里失去的权利从罪犯身上取走的执行者，即法官，并不是抽象的正义，而是一个存在者，正义只是他的一个变式。
应受惩罚的必然性是确定不移的，但正义的施行不是什么必然的东西，因为它作为活的东西的一个变式也可以消失，另一个变式可以进来；于是正义就成了某种偶然的东西；在作为普遍者、被思想者的正义与作为现实者、即在活的东西中存在着的正义之间，可以有一种矛盾；一个复仇者可以宽恕，可以放弃复仇；一个法官[可以不再]作为法官行事，可以赦免。
但这样一来，正义并没有得到满足；正义是不屈不挠的，只要法律还是最高的东西，就无法逃脱它，个体性的东西就必须被牺牲给普遍者，也就是说，它必须被杀死。
因此，设想法律可以在许多相同罪犯的一个代表身上得到满足，也是矛盾的；因为既然在他身上其他那些人也应当受完惩罚，他就是普遍者、是他们的概念，而法律无论是命令的还是惩罚的，都只有与特殊者相对立才是法律。

法律之具有其普遍性，条件就在于行动的人或行动是特殊的；而行动之所以是特殊的，是就它们被放在与普遍者、与法律的关系中来看，看它们是符合法律还是违背法律；就此而言，它们的关系、它们的规定性不能有任何改变；它们是现实的东西，它们是什么就是什么；已经发生的事不能变成没有发生，惩罚跟随着行为；它们的联系撕不开；如果没有办法让一个行为没有发生，如果它的现实性是永恒的，那就不可能有任何和解，即使受完惩罚也不行；法律倒是由此得到了满足，因为它所宣告的应当与罪犯的现实性之间的矛盾、罪犯想对普遍性做出的那个例外，被扬弃了。

但罪犯并没有与法律和解（对罪犯来说，这法律也许是一个异己的存在者，也许主观地在他心中，作为坏良心）；在前一种情形下，那个罪犯为自己造出来并武装起来对付自己的异己权力、这个敌对的存在者，一旦惩罚过，就不再对他起作用；当它按罪犯行事的同一方式反过来作用于他之后，它固然罢手了，却退回到威胁的姿势中去，它的形态并没有消失，也没有变得友好；而面对坏良心、面对对一种坏行为的意识、面对自己是个坏人的意识，所受的惩罚什么也改变不了；因为罪犯始终把自己看作罪犯，他对于自己的行为作为一种现实性没有权力，而他的这种现实性与他对法律的意识处于矛盾之中。

en: And yet man cannot endure this anxiety; from the terrible actuality of evil and the unchangeableness of the law he can only flee to grace, the pressure and pain of bad conscience can drive him again into a dishonesty, to seek thereby to run away from himself and thus from the law and justice, he throws himself into the lap of the administrator of abstract justice, to experience its goodness, from which he hopes that it may shut an eye at him, may look upon him otherwise than he is; he himself indeed does not deny his transgressions, but he makes the dishonest wish that the goodness itself deny his transgressions, and finds comfort in the thought, in the untrue representation, which another being makes of him.

And so there would be no return to the oneness of consciousness on a pure path, no sublation of the punishment, of the threatening law and of bad conscience, except a dishonest begging — if punishment must be regarded only as something absolute, if it stood under no condition and had no side from which, with its condition, it would have a higher sphere above it.
Law and punishment cannot be reconciled, but can be sublated in the reconciliation of fate.
zh: 然而人还是受不了这种恐惧；面对恶的可怕现实性和法律的不可改变，他只能逃向恩典，坏良心的压迫和痛苦又可以把他赶向一种不诚实，让他借此设法逃离自己，从而逃离法律和正义；他扑进抽象正义的执掌者怀里，想体验到它的善意，希望它对他睁一只眼闭一只眼，希望它看他看得和他本来的样子不一样；他本人固然不否认自己的过失，却怀着不诚实的愿望，希望善意自己否认他的过失，并且在一个想法里、在一个不真实的表象里找到安慰，这表象是另一个存在者对他形成的。
这样一来，就不存在沿着一条纯粹的道路回到意识的一体性的归途，也不存在对惩罚、对威胁人的法律和坏良心的扬弃，除非是不诚实的乞求——如果惩罚必须只被看作某种绝对的东西，如果它不处于任何条件之下，也没有任何一面，使它连同自己的条件在自身之上有一个更高的领域。
法律和惩罚不能被和解，却可以在命运的和解中被扬弃。

en: Punishment is the effect of a transgressed law, from which man has declared himself free, but on which he still depends and which he cannot flee, neither the punishment nor his deed.

For since the character of the law is universality, the criminal has indeed broken the matter of the law, but the form, universality, remains, and the law over which he [believed he] had become master remains, but appears opposed according to its content, it has the shape of the deed contradicting the previous law; the content of the deed now has the shape of universality and is law; this perversion of the same, that it becomes the opposite of what it was before, is punishment — in that man has loosened himself from the law, he still remains subject to it; and since the law remains as universal, the deed too remains, for it is the particular. Punishment represented as fate is of quite another kind; in fate, punishment is a hostile power, an individual, in which universal and particular are united also in the respect that in it the ought and the execution of this ought are not separated, as with the law, which is only a rule, something thought, and needs something opposed to it, something actual, from which it receives force.
In this hostile power, too, the universal is not separated from the particular in the respect in which the law as universal is opposed to man or to his inclinations as the particular.
Fate is only the enemy, and man stands over against it just as much as a fighting power; whereas the law as universal rules the particular, holds this man under its obedience.

The crime of the man who is considered as caught under a fate is then not a rebellion of the subject against his ruler, the running away of the servant from his lord, the freeing from a dependence; not a becoming living out of a dead condition, for man is, and before the deed there is no separation, no opposite, much less a ruling thing.
Only through a going out from the unified life, which is neither regulated by laws nor contrary to law, through a killing of life, is something foreign created.
Annihilation of life is not a non-being of it, but its separation, and the annihilation consists in this, that it has been turned into an enemy.
It is immortal, and killed it appears as its terrifying spectre, which asserts all its branches, lets loose its Eumenides.

The deception of the crime, which believes it destroys foreign life and thereby enlarges itself, dissolves into this, that the departed spirit of the violated life steps forth against it, like Banquo, who came to Macbeth as a friend, was not obliterated in his murder, but at the next moment nevertheless took his seat; not as a companion of the meal, but as an evil spirit.

The criminal thought he had to do with foreign life; but he has destroyed only his own life; for life is not different from life, because life is in the one divinity; and in his insolence he has indeed destroyed, but only the friendliness of life: he has turned it into an enemy.
Only the deed has created a law whose dominion now enters; this law is the union in the concept of the equality of the apparently foreign violated life and of one's own forfeited life.

Only now does the violated life step forth as a hostile power against the criminal and maltreat him as he has maltreated; thus punishment as fate is the same counter-action of the criminal's own deed, a power that he himself arms, an enemy that he himself made into an enemy for himself.
With fate a reconciliation seems even harder to think than with the punishing law, since, in order to reconcile fate, the annihilation seems to have to be sublated.

But fate has this advantage over the punishing law with regard to reconcilability, that it is located within the domain of life, whereas a crime under law and punishment [is located] in the domain of insurmountable oppositions, absolute actualities.

In this [domain] no possibility is thinkable of how the punishment could be sublated and the consciousness of the evil actuality disappear, because the law is a power to which life is subject, above which nothing is, above which not even the divinity is, for it is only the force of the highest thought, only the administrator of the law.
An actuality can only be forgotten, i.e. lose itself as something represented in another weakness, whereby its being would nevertheless be posited as enduring.
But with punishment as fate, the law is later than life and stands lower than it.

It is only the gap of life, the missing life as power; and life can heal its wounds again, let the separated hostile life return into itself again and sublate the botched work of a crime, the law and the punishment.112) From the point where the criminal feels the destruction of his own life (suffers punishment) or recognizes himself (in bad conscience) as destroyed, the effect of his fate begins, and this feeling of the destroyed life must become a longing for the lost life; what is missing is recognized as his part, as what should be in him and is not in him; this gap is not a non-being, but life recognized and felt as not being.

This fate felt as possible is the fear of it, and is a quite different feeling from the fear of punishment; the former is the fear of separation, a shyness before oneself; the fear of punishment is the fear of something foreign; for even if the law is recognized as one's own law, in the fear of punishment the punishment is something foreign, if it is not represented as fear of unworthiness; but in punishment there is added to unworthiness also the actuality of a misfortune, that the concept of man is lost113), i.e. that of which man has become unworthy; punishment therefore presupposes a foreign lord of this actuality; and the fear of punishment is fear of him — in fate, by contrast, the hostile power [is] the power of the life made hostile, thus the fear of fate is not the fear of something foreign.

Nor does punishment improve [him], because it is only a suffering, a feeling of powerlessness against a lord with whom the criminal has nothing in common and wants to have nothing in common; it can only bring about stubbornness, obstinacy in resistance against an enemy by whom to be suppressed would be a disgrace, because man would thereby give himself up.
In fate, however, man recognizes his own life, and his pleading to it is not pleading to a lord, but a returning and drawing near to himself.
Fate, in which man feels what is lost, brings about a longing for the lost life.

This longing can, if we are to speak of improving and of being improved, already be called an improvement, because, in that it is a feeling of the loss of life, it recognizes what is lost as life, as what was once friendly to it; and this recognition is itself already an enjoyment of life; and the longing can be so scrupulous, i.e. in the contradiction of the consciousness of its guilt and of life again beheld, still hold itself back from the return to life, however much the bad consciousness and the feeling of pain prolong it and urge it on every moment, in order to reunite itself with life not frivolously but from the depth of the soul, to greet it again as a friend.

In sacrifices, in penances, criminals have made pains for themselves; as pilgrims in hair shirts and barefoot, at every step on the hot sand, they have prolonged and multiplied the consciousness of evil, the pain, and on the one hand felt their loss, their gap, wholly through, on the other hand at the same time beheld this life wholly therein, though as a hostile one, and so made the re-adoption wholly possible for themselves; for the opposition is the possibility of reunion, and insofar as it was opposed in the pain, it is capable of being taken up again.

Because the hostile too is felt as life, therein lies the possibility of the reconciliation of fate; this reconciliation is therefore neither the destruction or suppression of something foreign, nor a contradiction between the consciousness of oneself and the hoped-for difference of the representation of oneself in another, or a contradiction between deserving according to the law and the fulfilment of it, [between] man as concept and man as actual.
This feeling of life that finds itself again is love, and in it fate is reconciled.

The deed of a criminal, considered in this way, is no fragment; the action that comes out of life, out of the whole, also represents the whole; the crime that is the transgression of a law is only a fragment, for outside it the law already is, which does not belong to it; the crime that comes out of life represents this whole, but divided; and the hostile parts can again go together into the whole.114) Justice is satisfied, for the criminal has felt in himself as violated the same life that he has violated.

The stings of conscience have become blunt, for their evil spirit has departed from the deed, there is nothing hostile left in man, and at most it remains lying as a soulless skeleton in the charnel-house of actualities, in memory.
zh: 惩罚是一条被违犯的法律的作用，人已宣布自己脱离了这条法律，但他仍然依赖于它，而且他逃离不了它，无论是惩罚还是他的行为。

因为法律的特征是普遍性，所以罪犯固然打碎了法律的质料，但形式、即普遍性留了下来，那条他[自以为]已成为其主人的法律留了下来，只是按内容显现为对立的东西，它具有与先前的法律相矛盾的行为的形态；行为的内容现在有了普遍性的形态，它就是法律；法律的这种颠倒，即它变成它先前所是的反面，就是惩罚——人既然把自己从法律中松脱出来，他就仍然受它支配；而由于法律作为普遍者留下来，行为也就留下来，因为行为是特殊者。被表象为命运的惩罚则完全是另一回事；在命运中，惩罚是一种敌对的权力，一个个体性的东西，在它之中普遍者和特殊者也这样结合着：在它之中应当和这个应当的执行不是分开的，而在法律那里，法律只是一条规则、一个被思想的东西，需要一个与它对立的东西、一个现实的东西，从那里得到强力。
在这种敌对的权力中，普遍者与特殊者也不是在下面这一意义上分开的，即法律作为普遍者与作为特殊者的人或其偏好相对立。
命运只是敌人，人同样作为战斗的力量与它相对而立；相反，法律作为普遍者统治着特殊者，把这个人置于自己的服从之下。
如果一个人被看作受命运纠缠，那么他的罪行就不是臣民对君主的反叛、仆役从主人那里的逃跑、对一种依赖的摆脱；也不是从死状态中活过来，因为人是存在着的，而且在行为之前没有分离，没有对立的东西，更没有一个统治的东西。
只有通过走出那既不守法律规范、也不违法的一体的生命，通过杀死生命，才造出一个异己的东西。
生命的毁灭不是它的非存在，而是它的分离，毁灭就在于它被改造成了敌人。
它是不死的，被杀死时它显得像是它那吓人的幽灵，这幽灵主张它所有的枝条，放出它的欧墨尼得斯。
罪行的欺骗——它以为摧毁了异己的生命，并因此扩大了自己——化解为这样的情形：被伤害的生命的离去的精神出现在它面前，就像班柯，他作为朋友来到麦克白那里，并没有在他的谋杀中被消灭，而是在紧接着的一刻还是坐上了自己的位子；不是作为宴席上的同伴，而是作为一个恶灵。
罪犯以为他面对的是异己的生命；但他毁掉的只是他自己的生命；因为生命与生命没有区别，因为生命在那唯一的神性之中；而他在自己的狂妄中固然进行了摧毁，但摧毁的只是生命的友善：他把生命变成了敌人。
只有行为才造出了一条法律，这条法律的统治现在开始了；这条法律就是概念中的结合，即表面上异己的、被伤害的生命与自己的、已被罚没的生命之间的等同。
直到现在，被伤害的生命才作为敌对的权力出现在罪犯面前，像他虐待过的那样虐待他；所以惩罚作为命运，就是罪犯自己的行为的同一种反作用，是他自己武装起来的一种权力，是他自己使之成为自己敌人的一个敌人。
与命运和解，似乎比与惩罚的法律和解更难设想，因为要和解命运，似乎就必须把毁灭扬弃掉。
但在可和解性方面，命运比惩罚的法律占优的地方在于：命运处在生命的领域之内，而法律和惩罚之下的罪行[则处在]不可克服的对立、绝对的现实性的领域之内。
在这个领域里，想不出任何可能性让惩罚被扬弃、让对恶的现实性的意识消失，因为法律是一种权力，生命服从于它，没有什么在它之上，连神性本身也不在它之上，因为神性只是最高思想的强力，只是法律的执掌者。
一种现实性只能被遗忘，也就是说，在另一种软弱中作为被表象的东西消失掉，而这样一来，它的存在倒还是被设定为持续存在的。
但在作为命运的惩罚这里，法律比生命更晚，也比生命更低。

它只是生命的缺口，是作为权力的缺失的生命；而生命可以重新治好它的伤口，让分离出去的敌对生命重新回到自身之中，并扬弃一桩罪行的拙劣制品，即法律和惩罚。112）从罪犯感到自己生命被毁灭（即遭受惩罚）或在（坏良心中）认识到自己被毁灭的那一点起，他的命运的作用就开始了，而这种对被毁灭的生命的感受必然会变成对失去的生命的渴望；缺失的东西被认作他的一部分，被认作本应在他之中而并不在他之中的东西；这个缺口不是一种非存在，而是被认作并被感受为非存在的生命。

这种被感受为可能的命运，就是对它的恐惧，是一种与对惩罚的恐惧完全不同的感受；前者是对分离的恐惧，是对自己的一种畏避；对惩罚的恐惧是对一个异己东西的恐惧；因为即使法律被认作自己的法律，在对惩罚的恐惧中，惩罚仍是一个异己的东西，除非它被表象为对无价值的恐惧；但在惩罚中，除了无价值，还加上了一种不幸的现实性，即人的概念丧失了113），也就是人已变得不配的那个东西；所以惩罚预设了一个占有这种现实性的异己主人；而对惩罚的恐惧就是对他的恐惧——在命运中则相反，敌对的权力就是那被变成敌对方的生命的权力，所以对命运的恐惧不是对一个异己东西的恐惧。
惩罚也不能使人变好，因为它只是一种痛苦，一种面对一个主人的无力感，罪犯与这个主人没有共同之处，也不想有共同之处；它只能造成固执，造成对一个敌人抵抗到底的执拗，因为被这个敌人压制会是耻辱，那样人就放弃了自己。
但在命运中，人认识到自己的生命，他对命运的祈求不是对一个主人的祈求，而是一种返回自身、接近自身。
人在其中感到失去的东西的那种命运，引起对失去的生命的渴望。

如果要谈变好和被改善，这种渴望已经可以叫作一种改善，因为它既然是生命丧失的感受，就把失去的东西认作生命，认作曾经对它友好的东西；而这种认识本身就已经是一种对生命的享受；这种渴望又可以如此认真，也就是说，在对自己罪责的意识与重新被直观到的生命之间的矛盾中，仍然不肯回到生命那里去，无论坏意识和痛苦的感受怎样把它拖长，怎样每一刻都刺激它，为的是不轻率地与生命重新结合，而是从灵魂深处重新与它结合，重新把它当作朋友来问候。
在献祭中、在苦修中，罪犯们给自己制造了痛苦；作为朝圣者，穿着粗毛衬衣、光着脚，每踩上滚烫的沙子一步，就把对恶的意识、把痛苦拖长并加倍，一方面把自己的丧失、自己的缺口整个地感受透了，另一方面同时在其中整个地直观到这生命，尽管是作为敌对的，从而为自己使重新接纳完全成为可能；因为对立是重新结合的可能性，而既然它在痛苦中被对立起来，它就能够重新被接纳。
因为敌对的东西也被感受为生命，命运之能够和解就在于此；所以这种和解既不是对一个异己东西的摧毁或压制，也不是自我意识与所希望的另一存在者对自己的表象有所不同之间的那种矛盾，也不是按法律应得与法律的履行之间的矛盾，[即]作为概念的人与作为现实的人之间的矛盾。
这种重新找到自身的生命的感受就是爱，命运在爱中和解。
以这种方式来看，罪犯的行为不是一个碎片；从生命、从整体中出来的行动，也把整体呈现出来；作为违法行为的罪行只是一个碎片，因为在它之外已经有法律，而法律并不属于它；从生命中出来的罪行则把这一整体呈现出来，但呈现为分裂的；而那些敌对的各部分可以重新合为整体。114）正义得到了满足，因为罪犯已经在自身中感到，他所伤害的那同一个生命受到了伤害。
良心的芒刺变钝了，因为它们的恶的精神已经从行为中离去，人身上再也没有敌对的东西，它最多只还作为一具无灵魂的骸骨，躺在现实性的骸骨房里、在记忆里。

en: But fate has a more extensive domain than punishment; it is also provoked by guilt without crime, and is therefore infinitely stricter than punishment; its strictness often seems to pass over into the most crying injustice, when it comes forward all the more terribly in the face of the most exalted guilt, the guilt of innocence.

For since the laws are only thought unions of oppositions, these concepts by far do not exhaust the many-sidedness of life; and punishment exercises its dominion only insofar as life has come to consciousness, where a separation has been united in the concept; but over the relations of life that are not dissolved, over the sides of life that are given as livingly united, beyond the limits of the virtues, it exercises no power.

Fate, by contrast, is incorruptible and unlimited, like life; it knows no given relations, no differences of standpoint, of situation, no district of virtue; where life is injured, be it ever so lawfully, ever so much done with self-satisfaction, there fate steps in, and one can therefore say, innocence has never suffered, every suffering is guilt.

But the honor of a pure soul is all the greater, the more consciousness it has injured life in order to preserve the highest, and the crime is all the blacker, the more consciousness an impure soul injures life.
zh: 但命运的地盘比惩罚更广；没有罪行的罪责也会刺激它，所以它比惩罚无限地更严厉；当它面对最高的罪责、也就是无辜者的罪责而表现得越发可怕时，它的严厉往往显得要变成最刺眼的不义。
因为法律只是被思考出来的、各种对立的结合，所以这些概念远远没有穷尽生命的多面性；惩罚只在生命达到意识、分离已在概念中被结合起来的地方行使它的统治；但对于那些没有被消解的生命关联，对于那些活生生地结合着被给予的生命侧面，超出了美德的界限之外，它就没有任何力量。
命运却像生命一样不受收买、没有界限；它不承认任何被给予的关系，不承认立场、处境上的差别，也没有美德的领地；哪里生命受了伤害——哪怕伤害得多么合乎权利，哪怕做得多么心安理得——命运就在哪里出现，因此可以说：无辜从来没有受过苦，每一份痛苦都是罪责。
但一个纯洁灵魂的荣誉，随着它为了保住最高者而多么有意识地伤害了生命而越发伟大，而一个不纯的灵魂多么有意识地伤害生命，罪行就多么漆黑。

en: A fate seems to arise only through another's deed, but this is [however] only the occasion; what it arises through, however, is the manner of receiving and of reacting to the alien deed.

Whoever suffers an unjust attack can defend himself and assert himself and his right, or else not defend himself; with his reaction, be it patient pain or struggle, his guilt, his fate begins; in both cases he suffers — no punishment, but no wrong either; in struggle he holds fast to his right and asserts it; in enduring too he does not give up his right; his pain is the contradiction that he recognizes his right but does not have the power to hold fast to it in actuality; he does not fight for it, and his fate is his will-lessness.
Whoever fights for what is in danger has not lost that for which he fights.115)

But by the fact that he enters into danger, he has subjected himself to fate, for he steps onto the battlefield of power against power and ventures himself against an other; courage, however, is greater than painful endurance, because the former, even if it is defeated, recognized this possibility beforehand, thus took the guilt upon itself with consciousness, whereas painful passivity merely hangs on its lack and does not oppose to it a fullness of power; but the suffering of courage is also a just fate, because the courageous man entered into the domain of right and of power; and therefore the struggle for rights is already an unnatural condition, just as much as passive suffering, in which there is the contradiction between the concept of right and its actuality; for in the struggle for rights too there lies a contradiction; the right, which is a thought, thus a universal, is in the attacker another thought, so there would be here two universals that would cancel each other out and yet are; likewise the combatants are opposed as actual, two kinds of living beings, life in struggle with life, which again contradicts itself.

Through the self-defense of the insulted party, the attacker is likewise attacked and thereby placed in the right of self-defense, so that both have right, both find themselves in a war that gives both the right to defend themselves; and [since they] thus either let the decision of right depend on violence and strength, although right and actuality have nothing in common with each other, they mix the two and make the former dependent on the latter; or they submit themselves to a judge, i.e., insofar as they are hostile, they give themselves up weaponless, dead; they renounce their own mastery of actuality, their power, and let a foreign thing, a law in the mouth of the judge, speak over them; thus they submit themselves to a treatment against which each party protested, in that they contradicted the violation of their right, i.e., set themselves against treatment by another.

The true [element] of both opposites, of courage and of passivity, is thus united in the beauty of the soul, so that from the former life remains but the opposition falls away; from the latter the loss of right remains but the pain disappears.
And so a cancellation of right arises without suffering, a living, free elevation above the loss of right and above the struggle.

The one who lets go of that to which another approaches him hostilely, who ceases to call his own what the other touches, escapes the pain over loss, he escapes being treated by the other or by the judge, he escapes the necessity of treating the other; whichever side of him is touched, he withdraws from it and leaves to the other only a thing that he has in the moment of the attack made into a foreign thing.
But this giving-up of his relations, which is an abstraction from himself, has no fixed limits.116)

(The more living the relations are from which a noble nature must withdraw because they are stained, since it could not remain in them without defiling itself, the greater is its misfortune; but this misfortune is neither unjust nor just, it becomes its fate only through the fact that it disdains those relations with its own will, with freedom; all the pains that arise for it from this are then just and are now its unhappy fate, which it has itself made with consciousness, and it is its honor to suffer justly, for it is so far exalted above these rights that it wanted to have them as enemies.
And because this fate lies in itself, it can [it] bear, stand over against it, for its pains are not a pure passivity, the superior power of a foreign thing, but its own product.)

In order to save himself, man kills himself; in order not to see what is his in a foreign power, he no longer calls it his, and so he annihilates himself while he wanted to preserve himself, for what would be under foreign power would no longer be he, and there is nothing that could not be attacked and that could not be given up.117) The misfortune can become so great that his fate, this self-killing in renouncing life, drives him so far that he must withdraw entirely into the void.

But in that man thus sets the most complete fate over against himself, he has at the same time raised himself above all fate; life has become unfaithful to him, but he not to life; he has fled it, but not injured it, and he may long for it as for an absent friend, but it cannot pursue him as an enemy; and he is vulnerable on no side, like the shamefaced plant he draws himself back into himself at every touch, and before he made life into an enemy for himself, before he provoked a fate against himself, he flees from life; thus Jesus demanded of his friends that they leave father, mother, everything, in order not to enter into an alliance with the degraded world and so into the possibility of a fate.
Further: whoever takes your coat from you, give him your cloak also; if a member offends you, cut it off.
The highest freedom is the negative attribute of the beauty of the soul, i.e., the possibility of renouncing everything in order to preserve oneself.
But whoever wants to save his life will lose it.
Thus with the highest guiltlessness the highest guilt, with exaltation above all fate the highest, most unhappy fate is compatible.

A mind that is thus exalted above the relations of right, caught up in nothing objective, has nothing to forgive the insulter, for he has violated no right of it, for it gave it up as soon as its object was touched.

It is open to reconciliation, for it is possible for it to take up again at once every living relation, to enter again into the relations of friendship, of love, since it has injured no life in itself; on its own side no hostile feeling stands in its way within it, no consciousness, no demand on the other to restore the injured right, no pride that would demand of the other the confession of having been beneath it in a lower sphere, the legal domain.

The forgiveness of faults, the readiness to be reconciled with the other, Jesus makes so decisively the condition of the forgiveness of his own faults,118) of the cancellation of a hostile fate of his own.
Both are only different applications of the same character of the soul.

In reconciliation with those who insult, the mind no longer insists on the legal opposition that it acquired against them, and in giving up the right, as its hostile fate, the evil genius of the other, it reconciles itself with him and has won just as much for itself in the domain of life, has made just as much life that was hostile to it into a friend, has reconciled the divine with itself, and the fate armed against itself by its own deed has dissolved into the breezes of the night.
zh: 一场命运看来只是由别人的行为产生的，但这〔不过〕只是诱因；真正产生命运的，是对这外来行为的接受方式和反应方式。
